rules.question: How is a long label cut to fit its space?
must_match: font->RenderChar(draw, size, ImVec2(IM_TRUNC(pos.x + kept_w), pos.y), col, font->EllipsisChar);
must_not_match: const std::string shown = ellipsize(label, w, ten_per_char);
label = "a";  // ends in â¦ when cut

owner_lines.why: ellipsize, the owner: the one ellipsis a cut ends in

rules.note: Cutting a label to end in "…": ImGui's own ellipsis renderer, its ellipsis glyph, the "…" bytes typed out as escapes, or a "…" typed straight into a string before any // comment. ellipsize is the one rule (no trailing space, an exact fit allowed); text_ellipsized cuts through it. The last alternative is built from the three UTF-8 bytes of "…", so this file holds no raw one in a pattern. Decided by: audit finding 70; D48, Q18 (phase 3 task O3b)

rules.question: Is a span on after this instant?
must_match: on = tg == Toggle::Start || tg == Toggle::Restart || tg == Toggle::On;
bool toggle_on(Toggle t) { return t != Toggle::Empty && t != Toggle::End; }
must_not_match: bool on = first == Toggle::End || first == Toggle::Restart || first == Toggle::On;

owner_lines.line_text: return t == Toggle::Start || t == Toggle::Restart || t == Toggle::On;

rules.note: "On before this instant" (End, Restart, On: the state entering a window) is a different question and is not flagged.

rules.question: Where is the far end of the highway?
must_match: const double far_time = now_s + speed * cfg.track.secs_future;
const double far_t = now_s + speed * T.secs_future;
must_not_match: const double far_t = far_time(cfg, now_s, speed);
rules.note: ---- phase 6 task J2-8: render callers and the Onyx numbers ---- The highway's far end is now plus speed times secs_future; time_to_z, z_to_time and the draw list's window all ask far_time. Decided by: audit finding 224; phase 6 task J2-8 (D54)

rules.question: Where does the track rectangle sit, and at what size?
must_match: const HighwayCamera cam = make_camera(cfg, static_cast<float>(w) / static_cast<float>(th));
return highway_span_at(cfg, width, height, static_cast<float>(std::max(1, height))).left - gap;
rules.note: The track rectangle: the size floor (below 1 counts as 1), the camera aspect (width over track height) and the bottom anchor (the track's top row is the image height less the track height). The last alternative is the renderer's old fade rectangle, which divided the track height by the image height; it now converts track_rect's top row to screen coordinates. Decided by: audit finding 221; phase 6 task J2-8 (D54)

rules.question: In what order does a polygon become triangles?
rules.note: A polygon becomes triangles as a fan from its first corner (Onyx's triangulate). load_obj's faces and the built flat and box meshes all push their vertices through push_fan. Decided by: audit finding 226; phase 6 task J2-8 (D54)

rules.question: Which X edge of a railing faces away from the lanes?
must_match: const float outer = right ? x2 : x1;
rules.note: Which end of a railing's X extent is its outer edge. railing_x owns the extent; railing_outer_x picks the outer end, and the SP end markers and highway_span_at ask it. A railing_x call with a literal side is how a caller picked an end by hand. Decided by: SPTRI derive-once review, finding 1 (D81)

rules.question: Where may a line break fall in a Preview text box?
must_not_match: for (const std::string& line : wrap_words(text, 0.0f, width_of, keep_last))
rules.note: Where a Preview text box's line may break: wrap_words walks the spaces, and widest_word takes the widest line it makes at width 0. Decided by: audit finding 75; phase 6 task J2-8 (D54)

rules.question: Whose numbers does the Preview draw with?
must_match: float secs_future = 1.35f;  // events this far ahead sit at z_future
int msaa = 4;  // mirrors Onyx's prefMSAA default
must_not_match: float secs_future{};  // events this far ahead sit at z_future
rules.note: The Preview's numbers live in assets/preview/3d-config.json alone; a PreviewConfig that was not loaded holds zeros. A field set to a number, or a brace initializer holding one, would be a second copy. Color's white and Vec3's origin are the types' own defaults, not Onyx's numbers, so their two member lines are left out. Decided by: audit finding 220; phase 6 task J2-8 (D54)
